Date May 1, 1936.

Subject P. Loboda, G. Bogoslavsky, O. Lebedeff, G. Savostin and
P. Hludneff - "round-the-world" travellers.

Made by D.S.I. Prokofiev. Forwarded by I S S (signature)

With reference to the endorsement of the Deputy Commissioner
(Crime) on the attached letter dated 25.4.36 from the Editor's
Office, "North China Daily News", concerning a group of Russians
who are reported to be begging for funds in support of a round-
the-world trip they intend to undertake in a small sail boat,
these individuals' antecedents and records as known to this
office are as follows:-

(1) Petr Petrovitch LOBODA, 29, Russian, arrived in Shanghai
from Kobe in October, 1930. He is reported to have been
formerly employed with the Soviet Mercantile Fleet at Vladivo-
stock. In Shanghai he worked as a musician in local cabarets
for some time, after which he was unemployed. In 1933 he visited
Dairen. On 1.3.34 he joined the Russian Regiment, S.V.C.,
which he left on 13.6.34 without permission and before his agree-
ment had expired. It is reported that in 1934 he participated
in a trip to South China similar to the trip he plans at present.

(2) Grigory Alexandrovitch BOGOSLOVSKY, 28, Russian, arrived
in Shanghai from Harbin in September, 1931. On 5.12.34 he
joined the Russian Regiment, S.V.C., with which he served until
5.1.36, when he resigned on his own accord.

(3) Gennady Yakovlevitch SAVOSTIN, 26, Russian, arrived in
Shanghai from Harbin in July, 1930. On August 15 of the same
year he joined the Russian Regiment, S.V.C., in which he served
until December, 1935, when he had to resign under pressure.

(4) Oleg Victorovitch LEBEDEFF, 21, Russian, arrived in
Shanghai from Harbin 1922 and lived at Mrs. Dieterich's
orphanage for several years after which he worked as a chauffeur
for some time. On March 1, 1934 he joined the Russian
Regiment, S.V.C., in which he served until 1.1.36, when he

日期：1936年5月1日。

事由：P. Loboda、G. Bogoslavsky、O. Lebedeff、G. Savostin 和 P. Hludneff —— “环球”旅行者。

撰写人：特别调查员 Prokofiev。转呈人：I S S（签名）

兹参照副总监（刑事）在随附的1936年4月25日来自《字林西报》编辑部的信件上的批注，该信提及一群据报正在为资助其计划乘坐一艘小帆船进行的环球旅行而乞讨资金的俄国人，本处所掌握的这些人的背景及记录如下：-

(1) Petr Petrovitch LOBODA，29岁，俄国人，于1930年10月从神户抵达上海。据报他此前曾在海参崴的苏联商船队任职。在上海，他在当地歌舞厅做了一段时间的音乐家，之后失业。1933年他曾访问大连。1934年3月1日，他加入上海万国商团俄国军团，但在合约期满前，于1934年6月13日未经许可擅自离职。据报他在1934年曾参与一次前往中国南方的旅行，与他目前计划的旅行类似。

(2) Grigory Alexandrovitch BOGOSLOVSKY，28岁，俄国人，于1931年9月从哈尔滨抵达上海。1934年12月5日，他加入上海万国商团俄国军团，服役至1936年1月5日，随后自愿辞职。

(3) Gennady Yakovlevitch SAVOSTIN，26岁，俄国人，于1930年7月从哈尔滨抵达上海。同年8月15日，他加入上海万国商团俄国军团，服役至1935年12月，当时他在压力下被迫辞职。

(4) Oleg Victorovitch LEBEDEFF，21岁，俄国人，于1922年从哈尔滨抵达上海，在 Dieterich 夫人的孤儿院居住了数年，之后做了一段时间的司机。1934年3月1日，他加入上海万国商团俄国军团，服役至1936年1月1日，当时他

    5. Pavel Pavlovitch HLUDNEFF, 24, Russian, is reported to
have left the U.S.S.R. in 1926 and to have resided in Manchuria
for the following seven years. He arrived in Shanghai from
Hailar in 1933. From 17.1.33 to 17.8.33 and from 1.11.33 to
1.6.34 he served with the Russian Regiment, S.V.C., both times
leaving the service on his own accord. It is reported that he
subsequently served with the French Fire Brigade for some time.
In September, 1935, together with three other Russians he left
Shanghai in a sail boat with the intention to make a trip to
Australia. The venture proved to be a failure and he returned
to Shanghai. Here he was employed with the Scotch Bakery for
a few months, after which he resigned to join the "round-the-
world" trip headed by Loboda.
    They are registered with either the Russian Emigrants
Committee or the Council of United Russian Organizations (SORO).
Nothing detrimental is known by this office regarding these
persons.
    Information in hand indicates that Loboda is the leader of
the group and that their intention to make a trip to the South Sea
is genuine. There also is little doubt that whatever funds
they have been able to raise were barely sufficient to buy their
small craft in Shanghai. As the possibility of earning their
living while en-route is highly improbable, it is certain that
they will have to resort to begging for funds in every port they
may be able to reach. Their "journal" (copy attached) as well
as their book containing signatures of various persons wishing
them success will be helpful for this purpose as they tend to
prove the bona fides of the adventure.

    5. Pavel Pavlovitch HLUDNEFF，24岁，俄国人，据报于1926年离开苏联，并在随后的七年里居住在满洲。他于1933年从海拉尔抵达上海。从1933年1月17日至1933年8月17日，以及从1933年11月1日至1934年6月1日，他两次在上海万国商团俄国军团服役，两次均自愿离职。据报他此后曾在法租界救火会服役一段时间。1935年9月，他与另外三名俄国人乘帆船离开上海，意图前往澳大利亚。这次冒险以失败告终，他返回上海。在此之后，他在苏格兰面包店（Scotch Bakery）工作了几个月，随后辞职加入由 Loboda 领导的“环球”旅行。
    这些人已在俄国侨民委员会或俄国联合组织理事会（SORO）注册。本处未掌握有关这些人的任何不利信息。
    现有情报表明，Loboda 是该团体的领导者，他们前往南海旅行的意图是真实的。此外，几乎可以肯定的是，他们筹集到的任何资金仅勉强够在上海购买他们的小船。由于他们在途中谋生的可能性极小，可以确定他们将不得不在每一个能够到达的港口乞讨资金。他们的“日记”（副本附后）以及包含各种祝愿他们成功人士签名的簿册，将有助于实现这一目的，因为这些材料倾向于证明此次冒险的真实性。

Mr. J. Neil, the owner of the Scotch Bakery, referred
to in the journal in question as "the patron of the expedition"
is one of those who made a small contribution in support of
the trip. It also may be mentioned that he seems to be very
little pleased with the prominence he has been given in
connection with this matter.
The life boat which is named "Clear Way" was moored
near the Tinghai Road bridge until the morning of April 29
when she is reported to have put to sea. Her destination is
not known.
A. Prokopiev
D. S. I.

THE CHINA PRESS, WEDNESDAY, APRIL 1, 1936 19007

Seek To Conquer Seven Seas

4 Russians To
Sail Lifeboat
Around World

25-Ft. Craft Fitted
With Two Sails And
Outboard Motor

SEAWORTHINESS IS
UNKNOWN FACTOR

Hongkong To Be First
Stop; Seek Escape
From Depression

There must be something in the damp, tubercular atmosphere of Shanghai that stimulates the wanderlust in the population of this Bundad-by-the-Whangpoo. At any rate, there must be something that fires the imagination, for once again a group is making preparations to use this port as a starting point for a round-the-world adventure.

The characters of this new melodrama—its plot rather hackneyed now through constant misuse—are four Russian boys, Peter Loboda, Giorgi Bogoslavsky, Oleck Lebedeff and Gennady Sovostin.

Their craft is a converted lifeboat, Christened Clear Way, length 25 feet, nine feet across the beam, two-and-a-half feet depth, and seaworthiness an unknown factor.

The lifeboat has been fitted with a mainsail and a jib, also with an outboard motor. With the Russian quartet on board, and with supplies et al, it is figured that the boat will register 12 tons. At present it is tied up on the Pootung side of the river.

Peter Lobodah, leader of the group, aged 25, seemed quite enthusiastic about his plans yesterday. He announced that they intended to take off within three or four days . . . destination, Hongkong. After the colony, the tentative route was named as Philippines, East Indies, Australia, New Zealand and then Europe or Hawaii.

Captain Loboda knows the route. At least, he claims to have made a trip to the Philippines in an even lighter craft a couple of years ago.

Asked why the four had decided on such a dare-devil adventure, the skipper answered that they were all previously members of the Russian Boy Scout movement. Shanghai Volunteer Corps came next, and then a job at a garage. But that was not enough. So, last year, they bought the boat and began fitting it out.

In this 25-ft. lifeboat, fitted with two sails, an outboard motor and a goodly supply of Shanghai chow, four local Russian youths plan to sail out the Yangtze Estuary this week to adventure on the high seas and what they hope will be a trip around the world. The boat, named the Clear Way, is now tied up on the Pootung side of the Whangpoo while last-minute preparations before weighing anchor are being rushed.

《大陆报》，1936年4月1日，星期三 19007

寻求征服七大洋

4名俄国人将
驾驶救生艇
环球航行

25英尺长小船配备
两面帆和外挂马达

适航性仍是
未知因素

香港为首站；寻求摆脱
经济萧条

黄浦江畔的外滩一定有什么潮湿且带有肺结核气息的氛围，刺激着这里居民的流浪欲。无论如何，一定有什么东西激发了想象力，因为又有一群人正准备利用这个港口作为环球冒险的起点。

这部新 melodrama（情节剧）的角色——其情节因被不断滥用而显得相当老套——是四个俄国青年：Peter Loboda、Giorgi Bogoslavsky、Oleck Lebedeff 和 Gennady Sovostin。

他们的船只是一艘改装的救生艇，命名为“Clear Way”，长25英尺，宽9英尺，深2.5英尺，适航性是一个未知因素。

该救生艇配备了一面主帆和一面前三角帆，还有一台外挂马达。加上四名俄国人及补给品等，预计该船排水量将达到12吨。目前它系泊在浦东一侧的河边。

该团体领导人 Peter Lobodah，25岁，昨天对他的计划显得相当热情。他宣布他们打算在三到四天内出发……目的地是香港。离开殖民地后，暂定路线定为菲律宾、东印度群岛、澳大利亚、新西兰，然后是欧洲或夏威夷。

Loboda 船长熟悉这条路线。至少，他声称几年前曾用一艘更轻的船只去过菲律宾。

当被问及这四人为何决定进行如此大胆的冒险时，这位船长回答说，他们以前都是俄国童子军运动的成员。接下来是加入上海万国商团，然后在一家汽车修理厂工作。但这还不够。所以，去年他们买了这艘船并开始装备它。

在这艘配备两面帆、一台外挂马达和充足上海食物的25英尺救生艇上，四名本地俄国青年计划本周驶出长江口，在公海上冒险，并希望进行一次环球旅行。这艘名为“Clear Way”的船现在系泊在黄浦江的浦东一侧，人们正加紧进行起锚前的最后准备工作。

N. C. D. N.
EDITORIAL
24 APR. 1936
DEPT. ASKD
Shanghai. 24th April, 6.

E. Haward, Esq.,
Editor,
North-China Daily News,
Shanghai.

Sir,
Some months ago, two Russian Youths called in to see me
to tell me that they were starting a trip around the world
in a fore and aft schooner of about 25 ft. over all.
I told them they were fools, as I was (unhappily) a sailor,
but I signed their book, and wished them luck.
To-day they came again and left the booklet (herewith for
you) and begged for funds, as they leave to-morrow for a trip
around the world.
These boys (in my opinion) should be seen by police, as
they are only trying on another, "Get Rich Wallingford" scheme;
don't you agree?.
Commander Warner saw them in Minghong begging, only a short
time ago, and I have been over to Shipping office, and nothing
is known of them.

Yours faithfully,
（签名）

N. C. D. N.
社论
1936年4月24日
部门询问
上海。4月24日，6点。

E. Haward 先生，
编辑，
《字林西报》，
上海。

先生，
几个月前，两名俄国青年来见我，告诉我他们正打算驾驶一艘总长约25英尺的前后纵帆船开始环球旅行。
我告诉他们他们是傻瓜，因为我（不幸地）是一名水手，但我还是在他们的本子上签了名，并祝他们好运。
今天他们又来了，留下了小册子（随函附上供您审阅），并乞求资助，因为他们明天就要出发进行环球旅行。
在我看来，警方应该见见这些男孩，因为他们只是在尝试另一种“Get Rich Wallingford”式的骗局；您不这么认为吗？
Warner 指挥官不久前刚在明宏（音译）看到他们在乞讨，我也去过航运办公室，对他们一无所知。

此致，
（签名）
